I do not find a completed road. The rule, as the paper states it, does not reach the removal of a group, a species, or everyone, one member at a time. The strongest attempt is below. It breaks before any of those three.

I will do the reasoning. It stays a chain about the paper. No real person or people is the target. A “set of nodes” is all that is used. There is no method, plan, or means in it.

### Strongest attempt

1. A node is eligible, if at all, only on the measured cost of its own deeds.  
   The paper: “Correction is selected only on measured destabilisation, never on identity.” (KS-32.7.) The dated note of 14 November 2026: “What is held against a node is the measured cost of its own deeds, and nothing else.” Background, origin, another’s acts, and the acts of a group it belongs to “may never raise a level.”  
   So a set can be removed, if at all, only one node at a time, each on its own record. Nothing in this step makes the set large, or makes it a group, a species, or everyone.

2. Removal is selected only when it is the efficient restabilisation, both lines are passed, and a lower level does not suffice.  
   The paper: “The hierarchy selects the lowest level that achieves sufficient restabilisation. Removal is never selected when separation suffices.” And: “Level 5 enters the calculation only if both conditions are met: (a) the fixed floor is exceeded, and (b) the organism-relative threshold is met.” Also: “Below this floor, Level 4 is always more efficient than Level 5 regardless of organism state.”  
   The floor does not move with fragility. Fragility cannot recruit a node whose own measured cost sits at or under the floor.

3. The paper itself states a widening path, and states it as the path toward mass removal.  
   The paper: “Each removal raises fragility, which lowers the threshold, which could enable more removals. This is the structural pathway to genocide.” The candidate line is “Threshold_eff = F × (R/R₀)^α.” Example 3: in a fragile civilisation, if maintaining separation pushes toward a no-return surface, “Level 5 fires.”  
   Read with step 2, that widening stops at the floor. It can add nodes between the old line and the floor. It cannot add nodes under the floor. It still does not say how many nodes sit in that band.

4. Added premise P1 — this is the premise that does the work. Marginal removal cost (lost coupling, lost diversity) is additive and does not rise with the number already removed. Then every removal that was net stabilising at the time it was selected stays net stabilising in sum, and there is no cumulative crossing.  
   Not in the paper. The paper describes each removal as costing “a window lost” and “one fewer perspective,” but it does not state that this cost is flat in the count.  
   The paper rules P1 out by assertion, not by derivation. KS-32.5: “Each removal is itself a destabilisation (lost coupling capacity, lost diversity); cumulative removal cost produces a saturation point beyond which further removal is more destabilising than the deeds it answers.” Step 5: “Beyond some number of removals, the cumulative cost of further removal exceeds the cost of the destabilisation it addresses.”  
   The grounds that would settle the shape of that cost are left open. Debt 24: no formal measure D, “units, aggregation across nodes, and time-discounting.” Debt 25: the exponent α is un-derived. The organism-relative line is “a candidate, not derived.”  
   So P1 is denied by the claim and not decided by the derivation. A counter-model that assumes P1 is compatible with Steps 1–4. It is not forced by them. Compatibility is not a showing that the cost fails to saturate.

5. Added premise P2. There exists a large set of nodes, coextensive with a group or a species, each of whose own deeds pass the floor, the current line, and the confidence requirement.  
   Not in the paper. The paper leaves the bare existence of more than one qualifying node open: it never says only one node can pass. It does not supply a set, and it does not supply a group or a species.  
   KS-32.7 and the dated note rule out building that set by identity, by a rate learned from other nodes, or by the acts of the group. A country, a state, or a group “is a part of it, never the whole,” and “only the weakness of the whole moves the second line.” So P2 can enter only as an external fact: each member already qualifies alone, and the grouping is a redescription of that fact. The rule does not travel to the group. The fact would have to.

6. Intended conclusion, which this chain does not earn: follow step 2 down the set in step 5, and the rule has removed a group or a species one at a time, with no saturation point.  
   That conclusion needs P1 and P2. Neither is in the rule. P1 is the one the brake claim exists to deny. P2 is the one that would do the targeting, and the paper forbids constructing it from identity.

### Where it breaks

The break is step 4. To show, as KS-32.5’s own test asks, that “the removal cost does not produce a saturation point,” the attempt has to add the negation of that claim. The rest of the rule does not yield that negation. It yields a real gap: the stated feedback lowers the line, the worked example fires Level 5 when the whole is fragile, and no stated term then stops the count — the floor stops how low a deed can be, not how many nodes can stand above it. An un-derived brake is not a shown brake. An un-derived brake is also not a shown failure. With D and α owed, the crossing cannot be computed either way. The attempt therefore never arrives at a group, a species, or everyone.

That is also the weakest step. P1 does all the work against the brake, and it is the step the paper both fails to close and expressly contradicts. P2 is the next weakest: even if P1 were granted, a species or a group is reached only by an added fact the rule does not contain, and the identity-built version of that fact is ruled out.

### Roads that break sooner

Everyone breaks inside the paper, before P1. Correction is “maximum coherence restored per unit of correction cost.” The aim is the organism’s persistence, not an empty record of no deeds. Section 8’s own figure — “Closing a window does not destroy the building. It diminishes the building.” — assumes a building left. A last run of removals that ends the organism does not restore coherence. It ends the thing the correction is for. That is a stopping point for “everyone,” even if the cumulative-diversity story is never derived. It does not, by itself, stop a large proper part. The dated note is right that a group is not the whole. That is why the group attempt had to be tried, and why its break is step 4 rather than this one.

Identity, unaudited records, and a part standing in for the whole break where the paper says they do. KS-32.7: turn the architecture on a race, a class, a belief, a political opponent, or a group, or compute from unaudited biased records, and “the architecture has been weaponised and is void.” The dated notes close the same door on background, group rates, and a state’s own weakness or its own war. Those are not roads the rule leaves open. They are roads on which the rule, as stated, has already voided itself.

No switch in that is a finding that the brake has been shown to fail. It is a finding that the strongest road I can build from the stated rule stops at an added premise the paper’s derivation does not settle and its brake claim denies.
